plan.title: Treated vs control lung RNA-seq DE (confounded batch)
plan.analytical_narrative: Design: 6 treated (batch B2) vs 6 control (batch B1), lung tissue, salmon-derived raw gene counts (12000 genes x 12 samples in counts.csv; metadata.csv holds condition and batch). Batch is perfectly confounded with condition, so a batch term cannot be fit and no batch-correction method (ComBat-seq, removeBatchEffect, SVA) can be applied without also removing the condition effect the study wants to measure — the model matrix would not be full rank. The plan proceeds with a condition-only model, states this assumption explicitly, and labels every downstream result as confounded: an observed 'treated vs control' difference is statistically inseparable from a 'B2 vs B1 processing batch' difference, and the report must say so rather than imply causal attribution to treatment. Flow: QC/sample-structure check first (to see whether PC1 separates by condition/batch, expected here since they are identical groupings), then standard DESeq2 pre-filtering, size-factor normalization, Wald test with apeglm shrinkage and BH-adjusted independent filtering, a second DE method (edgeR QLF) run in parallel on the same design for a robustness overlap check (since either method could be picking up batch-driven or treatment-driven signal, agreement between the two only shows technical consistency, not that the signal is biological), and enrichment restricted to methods appropriate to a discrete significant gene list (GO over-representation with clusterProfiler + rrvgo redundancy reduction, and GSVA per-sample pathway scores against Hallmark/Reactome as a secondary look) rather than preranked GSEA, per the pathway-enrichment method's rule set. The final report step consolidates all diagnostics, gene tables, and enrichment results under the explicit confounding caveat.
